task: Finish the Coloring minigame rebuild: render the 18-region robot as a tap-to-fill colouring page with a seven-colour palette, and make the child's finished artwork come alive as a nine-piece 2D paper puppet that HOPS around the 3D atelier.
context: esl-likes is a five-minigame 3D ESL game for Japanese elementary classrooms. The Coloring minigame currently has a three-colour palette and a three-region robot (body/arms/eyes) painted freehand and graded on a 72x72 pixel grid with a neatness margin. The owner wants one much more detailed robot, all seven lesson colours, tap-to-fill regions, and the finished robot hopping into the atelier as a paper puppet. THE PURE FOUNDATION IS ALREADY BUILT, TESTED AND VISUALLY ACCEPTED - robotDefinition.js (18 regions, 9 puppet pieces, pivots, hit testing, label placement), colorState.js (region colours, undo, eraser, guarded reset, completion), robotScoring.js (round selection, the four outcomes, stars) and robotRenderer.js (the one draw routine both halves use) exist with 66 passing tests. The controller rendered the robot in Chromium, looked at it, and fixed the three defects the previous pass recorded (label overflow, stubby arms, the shoulder plank). Do not redesign any of the four. This slice builds everything that touches a canvas, three.js or the DOM, and rewires index.js onto that foundation. Read .ai/coloring-robot-spec.md first; it is the frozen contract and it explains WHY pure region fill replaces freehand, why the puppet renders from shared shape definitions rather than cropped canvas pixels, and why the puppet hops rather than walks.
requirements: Read .ai/coloring-robot-spec.md first and treat it as the contract. Then read robotDefinition.js, colorState.js, robotScoring.js and robotRenderer.js - they are the frozen interface you build against, and their 66 tests must keep passing untouched.

picture.js: DELETE the old module's pixel-grid path entirely - buildRegionMap, GRID_WIDTH/GRID_HEIGHT, createPaintingSurface and all freehand painting. robotRenderer.js ALREADY draws the robot correctly (fills by region `order`, black line art redrawn over every fill, eyes above everything, labels placed by labelPlacement() and fitted by fitLabelFont()). Do not write a second renderer and do not change robotRenderer.js's draw order or label logic. What remains is the live surface: create the canvas, size it for devicePixelRatio, call drawRobot() on every change, and map pointer events to regions through regionAt().

Interaction is tap-to-fill only. A pointer event maps to a region through robotDefinition.regionAt(), which already handles the 44px touch floor - hovering or focusing highlights the whole logical region (pass `highlight` to drawRobot, which already draws it), and clicking fills it immediately. Do NOT require clicking only on painted pixels. Keyboard: Tab/arrow through regions and Enter/Space to fill, since the highlight already exists.

Render the round's instructions via robotRenderer, which already does this correctly: the starred region shows a bare star and NEVER the colour name, the two labelled regions show their small English colour word, and a label vanishes once its region holds the right colour. Your job is only to pass `round` and `colors` through.

Seven-colour palette UI: large swatches, strong selected state, wrapped or horizontal so they fit comfortably, Japanese labels. Add the four missing entries to UI.coloring.colors in src/config/lesson.js (みどり, ピンク, むらさき, オレンジ) alongside the existing あか/あお/きいろ. colorState.PALETTE and PALETTE_HEX already hold all seven; the config is the only place still short.
Add Undo, an eraser (clear one region), and a guarded やりなおす reset, all wired to the existing colorState methods, which already implement them. The guard must not be defeatable by a single mis-click.

Rewire index.js onto robotScoring: Done evaluates and branches on the four outcomes. FULL runs the cinematic. ALMOST plays a partial startup (eyes blink, antenna flashes, body wiggles, short buzz), shows もうすこし！, may indicate which LABELLED region is wrong, and returns to colouring. NOT_READY plays a failed startup (weak spark, tiny shake, power-down) and returns to colouring WITHOUT indicating anything about the starred region. INCOMPLETE shows its own friendly 'decorate a bit more' message and must never imply a colour is wrong. No outcome ever erases the child's work.

Delete the old scoring.js pixel-grid module and its tests once index.js no longer uses it. robotScoring.js replaces it. Check src/minigames/coloring/scoring.test.mjs and remove or port each test - do not leave dead tests asserting a grid that no longer exists.

Remove the old すてきな えが できたよ！ star-result panel from the success path. A generic results modal between correct colouring and the robot waking up is exactly what this pass is buying back. Stars are still awarded and still reach progression.awardStamp.

New robotPuppet.js: build a nine-piece flat paper puppet (head, antenna, torso, leftUpperArm, leftForearm, rightUpperArm, rightForearm, leftLeg, rightLeg). Texture each piece with robotRenderer.drawPiece(), which draws ONLY that piece's regions - REGIONS_BY_PIECE - onto a transparent canvas cropped to pieceTextureBounds(), using the same draw code as the colouring page. That is what guarantees the child's exact design survives, and it is why there is no canvas cropping, no texture atlas and no crop arithmetic to get wrong. Both functions already exist and are tested.

Make it visibly paper: thin geometry, a slight edge, a small drop shadow, a visible flat side at an angle, a slight tilt in the air. It must read as the child's drawing come alive, not a glossy 3D robot. Pieces rotate about robotDefinition.PIVOTS - no skeleton, no vertex deformation, no rigging.

LOCOMOTION IS HOPPING, NOT WALKING. This is the core animation direction and it replaces the walk cycle the spec used to describe - a flat cut-out attempting an articulated biped walk invites a comparison it loses, while the same pieces hopping read as a hand-puppeted paper toy. Four states, written plainly with no state-machine framework: IDLE (small up/down bob, subtle sway, occasional blink, antenna wiggle, slight side-to-side drift); STARTUP (anticipatory shake, quick bounce, eyes light up, arms twitch outward); HOP (crouch/compress, pop up and forward, airborne and tilted, land/squash, small recovery bounce, repeat - it must read as boing-land-boing-land); CELEBRATE (two or three quick hops, a happy arm flap, an excited antenna wiggle). Forward progress around the room happens through short hops, never a walk.

Light squash and stretch is ALLOWED and wanted, but it is scaling, not deformation: scale a piece's group non-uniformly - slight squash on landing, slight stretch on takeoff and in the air - with no axis outside 0.82 to 1.18 and the two axes compensating so a piece never changes apparent area by more than a fifth. Put that clamp in one exported pure helper and test it. A paper toy flexing, not rubber hose.

During a hop the limbs are deliberately loose: arms flap outward, legs stretch a little in the air, hands and feet lag behind the piece they hang from, and the antenna trails the head. Stylised looseness is wanted here - charming beats anatomically correct. Do not try to make it look like a real jump.

Cinematic on FULL, 3-6 seconds before control returns: glow, blink, antenna lights, arms twitch, a hop in place, peels off the paper, cut, drops onto the atelier floor, starts hopping. Keep it short enough for a classroom.

In the atelier the puppet roams a small authored loop (hop, idle, turn, hop) over a handful of points clear of the walls, easel, table and the artist NPC, and stays visible for the rest of the minigame. The wall frame shows the finished static artwork at the same time (the owner's option A). No pathfinding and no AI - authored points are enough.
Sound through the existing audio system only: fill pop, failed sputter, partial buzz, successful startup, and a small paper-tap on each landing. No new audio dependencies.

Add tests for the new pure parts: a piece's texture bounds match pieceBounds(); a rendered piece contains exactly its own regions in the child's colours (robotRenderer.test.mjs already has a recording context stub to copy); idle/startup/hop/celebrate transitions; a hop cycles crouch -> air -> land -> recover and returns to its starting height; the squash/stretch helper never leaves the 0.82-1.18 band on either axis; roam points stay inside the safe area. Keep the animation maths in pure exported functions so they can be tested without three.js. Do not test three.js rendering internals - a browser check is more useful there.

Append a dated entry to DESIGN_DECISIONS.md recording: that freehand painting and pixel-grid correctness are gone and why (twelve-plus small regions make a neatness margin impossible to tune on a touchpad); and that the puppet renders from shared shape definitions rather than cropped canvas pixels and why that is lossless rather than a rebuild-from-palette-values. The 2026-09-22 entry already there covers hopping, squash/stretch limits, label placement and the shoulder caps - do not repeat those.

Report: final region count, required vs free, the correctness and completion thresholds, how required labels work, how the child's artwork is preserved into the puppet, the piece structure, the four animation states and what each does, how much squash/stretch and limb looseness you used, what happens on each of the four outcomes, the scoring change, the unit test count, and anything you could not do as specified.
constraints: Do NOT modify robotDefinition.js, colorState.js, robotScoring.js or robotRenderer.js, or any of their four test files. They are the frozen, visually accepted foundation this slice builds against. If you believe one is wrong, say so and stop rather than editing it.
Do NOT add a second picture. One robot. The plan is explicit about this.
Do NOT redesign speech, mic, or mic-free behaviour, and do not rebuild the 3D atelier. Add only what the living paper robot needs.
Do NOT build a rigged, skinned or modelled 3D robot, and do not import a glTF. Flat textured quads rotating about pivots, with non-uniform group scaling for squash and stretch, and nothing more.
Do NOT add a walk cycle anywhere, even as a fallback or an option. Hopping is the only locomotion.
Free creative regions must never count as wrong and must never affect the score, in any colour combination. There is already a test asserting this; keep it true through the UI as well.
Never reveal the favourite colour. The starred region shows a star and nothing else, and no failure message may name or hint at the starred region's expected colour.

Work on the branch coloring-robot-alive, which is already checked out with a clean tree. Do NOT commit, push, stash, revert or git checkout anything, and do not touch files outside src/minigames/coloring/, src/dev/robot-preview/, src/config/lesson.js and DESIGN_DECISIONS.md without saying why.

src/dev/robot-preview/index.html renders the robot and the nine cut-apart pieces for visual judgement. You may extend it (for instance a panel drawing a few frames of a hop as stills) but do not break the panels it already has - the controller judges this pass through that page and the real game.
Source edits go through structured file writes. If a shell quoting or escaping attempt fails even once while editing a file, stop using the shell for that edit and write the file directly.
No new runtime or dev dependencies.
Do not attempt a browser playthrough; the sandbox cannot start this project's preview server. Behavioural acceptance is the controller's.

behavioralAcceptance.description: Play a full round in a real browser: hear a favourite colour, fill the starred region correctly, fill both labelled regions, decorate freely, press Done, and confirm the robot comes alive carrying the child's exact colours and HOPS around the atelier on articulated paper pieces with visible squash and stretch. Also the wrong-favourite, partial-wrong and not-decorated-enough paths. The worker sandbox cannot start this project's vite preview.
